descriptionChirho: Zechariah (Hebrew זְכַרְיָהוּ / זְכַרְיָה, 'The LORD has remembered'), a proper noun borne by numerous individuals in the Hebrew Bible, including: (1) Zechariah son of Jeroboam II, king of Israel (2 Kgs 14:29; 15:8,11); (2) several Levites and musicians in David's and Solomon's eras (1 Chr 9:21,37; 15:18,20,24; 26:2,11,14); (3) a prince sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the law (2 Chr 17:7); (4) a Levite son of Asaph in Hezekiah's reign (2 Chr 29:1,13); (5) an overseer of temple repairs under Josiah (2 Chr 34:12; 35:8); (6) Zechariah the prophet, son of Berechiah son of Iddo, who prophesied during the rebuilding of the temple (Isa 8:2; Zech 1:1; Ezra 5:1; 8:3,11,16; Neh 11:4,5,12; 12:16,35,41). All prepositional and conjunctional forms (and Zechariah, to Zechariah, for Zechariah) are inflectional variants of this single proper noun.
